from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the three displayed derived Hom objects: generic dg-quotient infrastructure through the recorded ancestry, specifically the finite-cone argument in the final step of lem-coef-dg-quotient-hom-cone. The triangulated structure is obtained from a general cone-closed module-category criterion, before proving invariance of the finite hull. Abstract dg-category axioms (A), (B), (C) supply the generic triangulation theorem used after the module and sign checks. Technical input: Simultaneous admissible replacement of a finite dg diagram.

title: Simultaneous admissible replacement of a finite dg diagram
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a small cochain dg category over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], with Hom differential $\partial$. Write $Z^0\mathcal A$ for closed degree-zero maps and $H^0\mathcal A$ for their classes modulo degree-minus-one boundaries. Assume (A) a zero object and dg binary sums, whose inclusions and projections are closed degree-zero maps satisfying the biproduct identities. Assume (B) dg functors $[n]$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, with $[0]=1$, $[n+m]=[n][m]$, and composition-compatible cochain isomorphisms $\mathcal A(x,y[n])\cong\mathcal A(x,y)[n]$, where $V[n]^j=V^{j+n}$ and $d_{V[n]}=(-1)^nd_V$. A sequence $u\xrightarrow{a}v\xrightarrow{b}w$ in $Z^0\mathcal A$ is called admissible when there are graded degree-zero maps $\pi:v\to u$ and $s:w\to v$ such that $\pi a=1$, $bs=1$, $a\pi+sb=1$, $ba=0$, and $\pi s=0$; its boundary is the closed map $\delta=\pi\partial s:w\to u[1]$ under (B). A map is an admissible monomorphism if it is the first arrow of such a sequence. Assume (C) that each closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$ has an admissible sequence $y\xrightarrow{i_f}c(f)\xrightarrow{p_f}x[1]$ with boundary $f[1]$. A homotopy equivalence is a closed degree-zero map with a closed degree-zero inverse modulo boundaries. For each integer $N\geq1$ and sequence of closed degree-zero maps $x_1\xrightarrow{f_1}x_2\to\cdots\xrightarrow{f_{N-1}}x_N$, there are objects $y_i$, admissible monomorphisms $j_i:y_i\to y_{i+1}$, and homotopy equivalences $r_i:y_i\to x_i$, with $y_1=x_1$, $r_1=1$, and $r_{i+1}j_i=f_ir_i$ as strict closed maps for $1\leq i<N$.
